purpose: Capture the actual background functions, native layout stalls and transport stages behind slow score updates in the next ordinary test export.
activation: Restart BTS and bts-testclient, then run the usual browser benchmark. The measurement browser automatically enables diagnosis before navigation. Ordinary user pages and BUP devices do not enable it.
implemented: An opt-in bounded page recorder retains each synchronous named UI-job/handler slice, unique job identity and owning game/update trace IDs. It also captures foreign work before a later score.

Native long tasks, long animation frames with source attribution/forced style-layout duration, and a 100ms heartbeat expose work outside the named handlers. Each long frame retains its 16 longest script entries and reports omissions.

The measured Chrome samples CPU at 2ms and rotates profiles every 15 seconds. Only three recent raw profiles remain; bounded per-outlier function summaries with source locations survive the entire run.
A separate control socket retains the earliest score receipt; per-point report rows link to an outlier window and preserve that control timestamp separately from the actual presentation timestamp.

Server output spans carry the exact connection identity. A separate score send_flush span records completion of the socket write, which is not claimed as browser delivery. Reconnect epochs are retained.
Score updates echo the diagnostic trace ID only when supplied by a test sender. Loaded versioned asset addresses identify the actual browser sources.
Non-score receipt transport projects metadata instead of deep-copying whole game/status payloads into DevTools. No CDP Network/WebSocket-payload tracing is enabled.

Shared UI jobs have unique IDs; completed observations are counted once under unique_ui_jobs. Existing ui_jobs explicitly remain receipt associations. Pending superseded observations do not consume the unique completed-job count.
Standalone older CPU diagnostic helpers disable the automatic profiler so they cannot race it.

limits.note: The first 120 outlier windows are retained, not silently replaced by the last ones. Over-capacity windows, overwritten page records, CPU coverage gaps and capture errors are exported.

native_fixture_proof.method: Actual Chrome CPU profiler, actual page code and PerformanceObservers; synthetic tournament, simulated identity response. No live BTS/BTP access.
assertions: The real page enables the flight recorder and exposes versioned asset paths
The measured page has its own server connection identity
The native point still completes its normal two-frame presentation receipt
Independent receipt timing triggers a named outlier window
The complete outlier window survives JSON export
The earlier unrelated task is present even though it is not the point’s dependency
The point handler is tied to the exact game and trace identifier
The CPU samples identify the deliberately blocking function and its source
Rotating the profiler retains the outlier across recording chunks
The report summary names the overlapping background job and sampled function
Native long tasks or long animation frames identify the actual stall
The diagnostic run retains existing game rows
No full WebSocket payload tracing is enabled
Diagnostic capture introduces no browser exceptions

limitations: Diagnostic sampling and serialization perturb the measured run. These results prove capture functionality, not improved latency or permanent compliance with the 100/150/50ms goals.
CPU times are sampled estimates; inclusive rankings overlap. Profile gaps, calibration uncertainty and unavailable native observer types must be inspected.
A control socket is a separate recipient; its timestamp is not the physical receipt time of the browser connection. Server connection IDs and send_flush spans make this distinction explicit.
Pure upstream delays can still require server traces: page captures trigger on browser work/control-gap thresholds, not every possible tablet-to-display latency.
No real tournament or external BTP was started, reset or modified during these validations. No full legacy-repository lint claim.
